title: Emit graph rollback lifecycle checkpoints
requires: Any development host plus one production driver implementing the current three-family interaction fixture
scope: Make the existing public-API interaction-graph lifecycle fixture emit the five formal three-family-partial-rollback observations required by adverse-capacity-three-family-v1, using the shared lifecycle reporting path introduced by F5-19.
acceptance: Emit installed, updated, partial-failure, recovery and replace-liquid observations for liquid, rope, soft-body, smoke and cloth with deterministic public-state and active-graph fingerprints.

Prove the rejected partial update preserves the accepted graph and every tracked resource, recovery restores the installed graph, and liquid replacement changes only the declared endpoint generation/state.

conformance/v1/lifecycle.py passes the three-family-partial-rollback case on every production driver advertising its required feature set; unsupported drivers remain explicit and no profile rule is weakened.
evidence: PASS: CUDA and Vulkan each produced 5/5 three-family-partial-rollback checkpoints with 0 lifecycle evaluator failures at clean source dbe5303.
PASS: CUDA/Vulkan graph and capacity CTests passed 4/4; graph fixture passed 10/10 repeated runs per backend with identical cross-driver observations.
PASS: Full adverse lifecycle profile passed 2 cases, 9 checkpoints, 0 failures on both CUDA and Vulkan; 75/75 conformance tests and embedded warning-clean compile passed.
